world.name: World style
world.text: Art direction: Free Kick Classics, an original football game set in believable football grounds. The environment is realistic: true-to-life stadium architecture and materials, natural turf, a crowd of individual people in real clothes, physically accurate light, shadow and weather, and real match-day detail such as blank perimeter boards, dugouts, stewards in plain hi-vis jackets, photographers behind the goal line, roof trusses and floodlights. Over the world sits only a light comic-print finish: faint halftone in the deepest shadows and a slight colour offset where things fall out of focus. The players, the ball and the action carry the full comic-book treatment, with bold hand-inked lines, halftone shading, speed lines and motion smears, so they pop off the real world. Dramatic light: golden hours, floodlights cutting through haze and rain, long shadows, drifting flare smoke. The goal frame, the ball and the players are the sharpest, clearest elements. Dynamic composition with bold camera angles.

sheet.name: Model sheet style
sheet.text: This is a reference sheet for 3D modelling and animation in Blender, matching the attached style reference. Characters are drawn in a comic-book 3D style: clean hand-inked contour lines, bold flat colour fills and light halftone shading. Props and architecture look realistic, with physically based materials. Orthographic views with no perspective distortion: every view at the same scale and standing on one shared ground line. Even, flat lighting with no cast shadows. Plain light grey background (#D8D8D8) with nothing else in frame. Do not draw numbers, arrows or labels.

texture.name: Texture style
texture.text: This is a texture for a 3D game. Photorealistic, viewed straight down, with perfectly flat, even lighting and no shadows or highlights. It must tile seamlessly on all four edges and fill the whole frame edge to edge, matching the attached style reference.

rules: Original design: not based on any real footballer, club, national team, stadium or brand, or on any existing film, comic or video game. No text, letters, numbers, logos, crests, sponsor marks, sound-effect lettering or watermarks anywhere in the image.

styles.world: Art direction: Free Kick Classics, an original football game set in believable football grounds. Render the environment realistically: true-to-life stadium architecture and materials, natural turf, a crowd of individual people in real clothes, physically accurate light, shadow and weather, and real match-day detail such as blank perimeter boards, dugouts, stewards in plain hi-vis jackets, photographers behind the goal line, roof trusses and floodlights. Give the world only a light comic-print finish: faint halftone in the deepest shadows and a slight colour offset where things fall out of focus. Give the players, the ball and the action the full comic-book treatment, with bold hand-inked lines, halftone shading, speed lines and motion smears, so they pop off the real world. Light it dramatically: golden hours, floodlights cutting through haze and rain, long shadows, drifting flare smoke. Keep the goal frame, the ball and the players the sharpest, clearest elements, and compose dynamically with bold camera angles.
styles.sheet: This is a reference sheet for 3D modelling and animation in Blender, in the look of the style keyframe. Draw characters in a comic-book 3D style: clean hand-inked contour lines, bold flat colour fills and light halftone shading. Render props and architecture realistically, with physically based materials. Draw every view flat and orthographic, like a technical drawing, at the same scale and standing on one shared ground line. Light it evenly from the front so every form reads clearly. Use a plain light grey background (#D8D8D8). The sheet holds only the drawings themselves.
styles.texture: This is a texture for a 3D game. Make it photorealistic and show the surface from directly above, evenly and flatly lit, so it reads as pure colour and detail. Make it seamless, so the left edge flows into the right and the top into the bottom, and fill the whole frame edge to edge, in the look of the style keyframe.

gemini.rules: Everything here is an original design invented for this game: the people, kits, ball, stadium and crowd are all new, and none of it comes from an existing film, comic or video game. Kits are plain fabric with abstract patterns, the ball carries only its panel pattern, and boards and signs are blank or abstract. Impact moments use graphic bursts and lines rather than lettering. Keep the whole image free of text, numbers, logos and watermarks.

prompts.title: Style keyframe: the stare-down
prompts.builds: The master look: lighting, colour grade, fog and sky for every scene.
prompts.tip: Generate three or four variations and keep the one you love. Attach it to every prompt after this one.
prompts.prompt: Cinematic wide frame of a penalty kick at golden hour in an original modern football stadium built on a harbourfront. In the foreground a kicker in a deep teal kit stands behind the ball on the penalty spot, seen from behind and slightly to one side. On the goal line the keeper, in a warm amber kit, crouches with his eyes locked on the kicker. Just behind the goal line, photographers crouch beside low blank perimeter boards, and behind them rises a steep two-tier stand packed with fans in scarves, with stewards in plain hi-vis jackets at the front. The far end of the stadium is open, framing the sea and a low sun that throws long shadows across freshly mown, striped turf. The floodlights are just flickering on, light haze hangs over the pitch, and a few strands of coloured flare smoke drift from the stand. The stadium, crowd and light look completely real; only the two players and the ball carry crisp hand-inked lines and halftone shading, like comic-book heroes standing in a real place. The mood is a held breath just before the strike.

prompts.title: Palette, materials and print patterns
prompts.builds: The Blender material library, the colour values every scene shares, and the halftone and ink shaders.
prompts.prompt: A tidy art-direction board on a dark charcoal background, using the colours of the attached keyframe. Across the top, a row of eight plain colour swatches: sunset gold, harbour blue, deep pitch green, chalk-line white, teal, amber, weathered concrete grey and floodlight white. Below them, six photorealistic material spheres in a row: striped natural turf, stitched ball leather, smooth modern ball synthetic, kit fabric with a woven texture, goal-net nylon, and weathered stadium concrete. Along the bottom, four square pattern swatches for the comic treatment of the players and the action: fine halftone dots, coarse Ben-Day dots, hand-inked cross-hatching, and offset colour misregistration.

prompts.title: Replay tracers: four inked ball flights
prompts.builds: The replay trajectory effect. In Blender the inked lines follow real flight paths exported from the game's own physics.
prompts.prompt: Four comic panels side by side, each a side-on replay of a football's flight in a stadium, with the path drawn as a bold inked curve, speed lines and a fading halftone trail. Panel one: a smooth bending curve for a curling shot. Panel two: an arc that dips sharply at the end for a topspin shot. Panel three: a nearly straight path that wobbles only in its last third, for a knuckleball, with jittery ink strokes. Panel four: a high, gentle lob for a chip.

prompts.title: Kicker turnaround
prompts.builds: The kicker model, rigged as a humanoid so animations can be shared and exported to Unity.
prompts.tip: If the views come back with perspective or shadows, reply in the same chat: “Same sheet, but flat orthographic views, evenly lit, every view the same height.”
prompts.prompt: Character turnaround model sheet of the kicker from the attached keyframe: an original young professional footballer with an athletic build and grounded, slightly stylized proportions, short curly dark hair, warm brown skin and determined eyes. Deep teal kit with a subtle tonal pattern across the shirt, white shorts, teal socks and gold boots. Three full-body views side by side: front, left side and back. A-pose, with arms angled 45 degrees down and feet shoulder-width apart.

Bottom row: four expressions from the front: calm focus, a sly bluffing half-smile, wide-eyed joy after scoring, and frustration after a miss. Shoulders up, with the same face shape and hair in every view.

prompts.title: Keeper turnaround
prompts.builds: The keeper model, on the same humanoid rig as the kicker.
prompts.tip: Start a new chat for the keeper so the kicker's features don't bleed into him.
prompts.prompt: Character turnaround model sheet of the keeper from the attached keyframe: an original goalkeeper, tall with long arms and large hands, grounded, slightly stylized athletic proportions, shaved head with a short beard, light tan skin and calm, intense eyes. Long-sleeved warm amber goalkeeper kit with darker amber elbow padding and a subtle tonal pattern, black shorts, amber socks, and well-worn goalkeeper gloves. Three full-body views side by side: front, left side and back. A-pose, with arms angled 45 degrees down and feet shoulder-width apart.

prompts.title: Keeper face and gloves
prompts.builds: The keeper's head, facial shape keys and glove model.

Bottom row: four expressions from the front: reading the kicker with narrowed eyes, a taunting grin, a roaring celebration, and quiet despair. On the right, a close study of one goalkeeper glove from the palm side and from the back.

prompts.title: Wall players

Show each player from the front and from the left side, standing in an A-pose, so there are six full-body views in one row.

The kicker's teal and gold kit from the kicker turnaround, an alternate kit in chalk white and violet, the keeper's amber kit from the keeper turnaround, and the wall team's deep crimson kit. Fabric weave and pattern detail clearly visible.

prompts.title: The referee
prompts.builds: The referee who sprays the 9.15 m line and pushes the wall back.

prompts.title: Run-up and side-foot strike
prompts.builds: The 1.5-second run-up and the placed shot.
prompts.prompt: Animation key-pose sheet of the kicker in the attached turnaround taking a penalty, seen from the side. Eight poses in a single row from left to right, evenly spaced: standing ready behind the ball; first step; mid-stride; long last stride with the planted foot landing beside the ball; kicking leg swinging back; side-foot contact with the ball; follow-through; landing and looking up.

prompts.title: Driven knuckleball strike
prompts.builds: The laces strike that feeds the knuckleball.
prompts.prompt: Animation key-pose sheet of the kicker in the attached turnaround striking a driven knuckleball, seen from the side. Eight poses in a single row from left to right, evenly spaced: ready; fast approach; planted foot; kicking leg cocked high; laces striking through the middle of the ball with the ankle locked; short, stabbing follow-through; landing; watching the ball fly.

prompts.title: Curler and trivela
prompts.builds: The inside-of-the-foot curler and the outside-of-the-foot trivela.
prompts.prompt: Animation key-pose sheet of the kicker in the attached turnaround, seen from the side, in two rows. Top row, four poses of an inside-of-the-foot curler, with the body wrapping around the ball. Bottom row, four poses of an outside-of-the-foot trivela, with the kicking leg swinging across the body.

prompts.title: The chip
prompts.builds: The soft chip that punishes an early dive.
prompts.prompt: Animation key-pose sheet of the kicker in the attached turnaround playing a soft chip down the middle, seen from the side. Six poses in a single row from left to right: ready; approach, slowing; planted foot; kicking leg swinging gently; foot scooping under the ball; a cheeky follow-through with the weight leaning back.

prompts.title: Stutter run-up
prompts.builds: The stutter bluff.
prompts.prompt: Animation key-pose sheet of the kicker in the attached turnaround doing a stutter run-up, seen from the side. Six poses in a single row from left to right: approach; a sudden hop and pause mid-run with the arms out for balance; a second small hop; the long final stride; the strike; follow-through.

prompts.title: Keeper ready and shuffle
prompts.builds: The keeper's idle stance and the shuffle bluff on the line.
prompts.prompt: Animation key-pose sheet of the keeper in the attached turnaround, seen from the front. Six poses in a single row from left to right: crouched ready stance on the goal line; shuffle step to his left; shuffle step to his right; arms spread wide to look big; bouncing on his toes; set position a moment before the dive.

prompts.title: Keeper dives: low, middle, top corner
prompts.builds: The dives, mirrored in Blender for the other side. Early and late dives are the same poses with different timing.
prompts.prompt: Animation key-pose sheet of the keeper in the attached turnaround, seen from the front as the kicker sees him, in three rows of four poses, all diving to the same side. Top row, a low dive to the bottom corner. Middle row, a dive at waist height. Bottom row, a full-stretch leap to the top corner. Each row runs from left to right: push-off, take-off, full stretch at the height of the ball, landing.

prompts.title: Stay big, catch and parry
prompts.builds: Staying big, catches and parries.
prompts.prompt: Animation key-pose sheet of the keeper in the attached turnaround, seen from the front. Six poses in a single row from left to right: staying big in a star shape with arms and legs spread; catching a ball against his chest; smothering a low ball on the ground; a one-handed fingertip tip over the bar; a two-fisted punch; getting back up from the ground.

prompts.title: The wall
prompts.builds: Wall set-up, jump, brace and the lying man for Wall Wars and the Classics cards.
prompts.prompt: Animation key-pose sheet of the wall players in the attached sheet, seen from the side. Eight poses in a single row from left to right: lining up shoulder to shoulder; hands covering in the set position; crouching before the jump; jumping together with arms down; landing; one player staying grounded to block a low shot; one player lying flat on the ground behind the wall; turning to watch the ball.

prompts.title: Celebrations and dejection
prompts.builds: The after-kick reactions for both players.
prompts.prompt: Animation key-pose sheet in two rows. Top row, the kicker from the kicker turnaround, four poses: a knee slide, an arms-wide aeroplane run, a finger to the lips, and hands on head after a miss. Bottom row, the keeper from the keeper turnaround, four poses: a roaring fist pump, pointing to the crowd, lying face down after conceding, and standing with hands on hips.

prompts.title: Three era balls
prompts.builds: The three balls, each paired with its era's physics in the game.
prompts.prompt: Orthographic reference of three original footballs in one row, each shown from the front and from the side. A 1970s ball of hand-stitched brown leather in the classic 32-panel pattern of hexagons and pentagons, slightly worn and scuffed. A 1990s glossy white ball with bold original curved-triangle graphics in black and gold. A modern lightweight ball with smooth bonded panels and an original pattern of sweeping teal and gold strokes.

prompts.title: Goal frame and net
prompts.builds: The goal to real dimensions, with a net that ripples and bulges on a goal.
prompts.prompt: Orthographic reference of a full-size football goal, front view and side view next to each other: slim, rounded white posts and crossbar, a deep net held out by thin back supports, and realistic white nylon net mesh. Add a close-up inset of the net knots in the corner.

prompts.title: Goal end, plan view
prompts.builds: The pitch layout and the goal-end perimeter. In Blender the pitch is built to regulation dimensions, so this checks the look of the lines and the run-off.
prompts.prompt: Top-down orthographic plan view of one end of a real football pitch, as precise as an architect's drawing: the goal line with the goal centred on it, the goal area, the penalty area, the penalty spot and the penalty arc, both corner arcs with their flags, and a curved line of white vanishing spray marking a wall 9.15 m from a free-kick position. Beyond the goal line, the grass run-off, the low perimeter boards and the front row of the stand. This view fills the frame with the pitch instead of the grey background.

prompts.title: Floodlights through the eras
prompts.builds: One floodlight design per era.
prompts.prompt: Three original stadium floodlight designs side by side, all seen from the front: a 1970s lattice steel pylon topped with a dense grid of lamps, a 1990s angular tower with rectangular lamp banks, and a modern floodlight ring set into the edge of a stadium roof.

prompts.title: The harbour stadium from above
prompts.builds: The layout and scale of the first playable ground.
prompts.prompt: Aerial three-quarter view of the harbourfront stadium from the attached keyframe at golden hour: a modern bowl with a sweeping translucent roof, three closed sides and one open end looking out over a harbour with moored fishing boats, a lighthouse on the breakwater, and the sun setting over the sea. Old brick warehouses and narrow streets surround the stadium, with fans streaming in. The roof trusses, floodlights, dugouts, perimeter boards and the full set of pitch markings are clearly visible. One end of the pitch, with its goal, is in the foreground.

prompts.title: Game camera: behind the ball
prompts.builds: The main kicker camera, framed for a phone.
prompts.prompt: The game camera's view from just behind and above the ball on the penalty spot, looking at the goal in the attached stadium. The keeper is set on his line. The whole penalty area, goal area and penalty arc are visible on the grass, photographers crouch behind the blank boards beyond the goal line, the steep stand behind the goal is packed with fans and scarves, and the evening sky glows above the roof. Framed for a phone held upright: the goal fills the upper half, and the ball sits in the lower third with clear space around it.

prompts.builds: The keeper camera, framed for a phone.

Behind the kicker, the open end of the stadium frames the harbour and the setting sun. Framed for a phone held upright, with the kicker small and central and the goal posts just out of frame on either side.

prompts.builds: Stand geometry and the crowd shader.

Both are lit by low golden sunlight with bold ink shadows, and the real stadium behind them falls softly out of focus with a slight colour offset. The tension of two friends trying to read each other.

Graphic impact lines burst outward from the net.

prompts.title: The fingertip save
prompts.builds: The slow-motion save, with water spray under the floodlights.

A spray of water flies off the ball and his gloves, each droplet catching the light, and the crowd behind falls softly out of focus with a slight colour offset. His body shows a motion smear and a few overlapping ink outlines from the dive.

pitch.name: Pitch markings
pitch.use: Every prompt that shows the pitch
pitch.chatgpt: Pitch markings must follow the Laws of the Game exactly and be drawn perfectly: one set of crisp, continuous white lines about 12 cm wide, dead straight, meeting at clean right angles, never wobbling, doubling, fading or breaking. The goal stands centred on the goal line, its posts 7.32 m apart and 2.44 m high. The goal area is a box 5.5 m deep and 18.32 m wide, two and a half goal-widths across. The penalty area is a box 16.5 m deep and 40.32 m wide, five and a half goal-widths across. There is exactly one penalty spot, 11 m from the goal line, two-thirds of the way out to the edge of the penalty area. The penalty arc is the part of a 9.15 m circle around the spot that lies outside the penalty area, bulging 3.65 m beyond its edge. Corner arcs have a 1 m radius. Beyond the touchlines and goal lines there is a clean strip of grass run-off before the low perimeter boards and the stands. Mowing stripes are even and parallel to the goal line. Every line lies flat on the ground in correct perspective. The measurements are for accuracy only: draw no dimension lines, numbers or labels.
pitch.gemini: Draw the pitch markings exactly to regulation proportions and with perfect precision: a single set of crisp, continuous white lines about 12 cm wide, perfectly straight, meeting at clean right angles and lying flat on the grass in correct perspective. The goal stands centred on the goal line, its posts 7.32 m apart and 2.44 m high. The goal area is a box 5.5 m deep and 18.32 m wide, about two and a half goal-widths across. The penalty area is a box 16.5 m deep and 40.32 m wide, about five and a half goal-widths across. A single penalty spot sits 11 m from the goal line, two-thirds of the way out to the edge of the penalty area. The penalty arc is the part of a 9.15 m circle around the spot that lies outside the penalty area, curving 3.65 m beyond its edge. Corner arcs have a 1 m radius. A clean strip of grass run-off surrounds the pitch before the low perimeter boards and the stands, and the mowing stripes run evenly, parallel to the goal line. The measurements guide the proportions only; the image shows just the white lines on the grass.
